claim_verdicts.evidence: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Infrastructure/DonHangDbContext.cs` lines 9-14: Customers, Products, Orders, OrderItems, Payments, Notifications, each expression-bodied over `Set<T>()`. Line 10 is exactly `public DbSet<Product> Products => Set<Product>();` — the string §5 quotes inline. `db/schema.sql` at the same tag has exactly six CREATE TABLE statements (products, customers, orders, order_items, payments, notifications), so §5's "one `DbSet<T>` property per table" holds. Tag stage-1 -> commit 4fca60a.

refs/efcore-docs/entity-framework/core/index.md: "EF Core can serve as an object-relational mapper (O/RM), which: Enables .NET developers to work with a database using .NET objects. Eliminates the need for most of the data-access code that typically needs to be written."; "A model is made up of entity classes and a context object that represents a session with the database. The context object allows querying and saving data."; "Instances of your entity classes are retrieved from the database using Language Integrated Query (LINQ)."

Verbatim, refs/efcore-docs/entity-framework/core/modeling/entity-properties.md line 30 ("Column names"): "By convention, when using a relational database, entity properties are mapped to table columns having the same name as the property." Followed by "If you prefer to configure your columns with different names…" with Data Annotations and Fluent API tabs. No built-in casing convention: core/extensions/index.md lists EFCore.NamingConventions as a third-party plugin for snake_case; grep of what-is-new/ef-core-10.0/ for "snake|naming convention" returns nothing.

`git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs` lines 17-22 are character-for-character the lesson's first code block: `public sealed class Product { public int Id { get; set; } public required string Name { get; set; } public int PriceVnd { get; set; } }`. Exactly three properties, no attributes, no base class; the file's only using-free header is `namespace DonHang.Domain;` — nothing referring to EF Core or a database.

DonHangDbContext.cs lines 30-36 match the lesson's second block character-for-character, indentation included: `modelBuilder.Entity<Product>(e => { e.ToTable("products"); e.Property(p => p.Id).HasColumnName("id"); e.Property(p => p.Name).HasColumnName("name"); e.Property(p => p.PriceVnd).HasColumnName("price_vnd"); });`. Same shape as refs/efcore-docs samples/core/Modeling/EntityProperties/FluentAPI/ColumnName.cs (`modelBuilder.Entity<Blog>().Property(b => b.BlogId).HasColumnName("blog_id")`); ToTable per modeling/entity-types.md "Table name".

claim_verdicts.evidence: Live: `docker exec donhang-db psql -U donhang -d donhang -c 'select "PriceVnd" from products'` -> `ERROR:  column "PriceVnd" does not exist` + `HINT:  Perhaps you meant to reference the column "products.price_vnd".` An error, not a silent null/0. issues.text: The quoted error text is the unaliased form. EF Core's generated SQL aliases the table (`FROM products AS p`), so the message a reader would actually hit names the alias. Verified live: `select "PriceVnd" from products` -> `ERROR:  column "PriceVnd" does not exist`; `select p."PriceVnd" from products as p` -> `ERROR:  column p.PriceVnd does not exist`. The failure itself (Postgres 42703, at query time, loudly) is right; only the literal string is narrower than what EF Core would produce.
issues.quote: the query would fail at runtime — `column "PriceVnd" does not exist` — because the table only has `price_vnd`
issues.fix: Either drop the literal and write "…and the query would fail at runtime, because the table only has `price_vnd`", or keep it non-literal: "PostgreSQL answers with an error saying the column `PriceVnd` does not exist". If the literal stays, extend claim 7 to record that the verified message came from a query without a table alias.

issues.text: Unlisted behaviour claim about `FindAsync`. Claim 8 covers LINQ deferred execution, not `Find`/`FindAsync`, which has a documented exception: refs/efcore-docs/.../change-tracking/entity-entries.md: "Find first checks if the entity is already tracked, and if so returns the entity immediately. A database query is only made if the entity is not tracked locally." The sentence is true as written for `Get(int id)` (the request-scoped `DonHangDbContext` is tracking nothing yet), but the ledger never records it, so it was never checked.
issues.quote: `Get(int id)`'s `FindAsync(id)` call is what turns `db.Products` into a real row read from PostgreSQL
issues.fix: Add a claim to .meta.json (kind `behavior`, version_key `efcore`, section 6) quoting entity-entries.md: "Find first checks if the entity is already tracked… A database query is only made if the entity is not tracked locally." Lesson wording can stay unchanged.

issues.text: Stated as a property of EF Core mapping, but it is this project's chosen direction. refs/efcore-docs/entity-framework/core/index.md lists both: "Generate a model from an existing database. Hand-code a model to match the database. Once a model is created, use EF Migrations to create a database from the model." And in this very repo the model does produce schema — stage-1 Program.cs runs `context.Database.Migrate()` over the `InitialCreate` migration, which backend.l1.migrations teaches two lessons later. Unconditioned, the sentence sets up a contradiction.
